result.title: DIVA: Dual-Space Intent-Aware Visual Attenuation for Vision-Language-Action Policies
result.summary: Vision-language-action (VLA) policies typically feed dense visual patch tokens into a language-action backbone, preserving scene context but offering no explicit mechanism to regulate how strongly different visual tokens influence policy computation. We introduce DIVA, a Dual-Space Intent-Aware Visual Attenuation module with an anchor-then-attenuate design. DIVA combines high-level task intent with low-level visual evidence to estimate patch-wise relevance anchors, then applies them in two complementary spaces: it reweights projected visual tokens before backbone entry and persistently attenuates low-relevance visual states within the backbone. DIVA preserves the full visual token sequence and requires no external grounding supervision. On LIBERO, DIVA improves OpenVLA-OFT from 96.6% to 98.0% average success and raises its zero-shot LIBERO-Plus score from 69.6 to 72.6. Real-world experiments further show consistent gains under task-irrelevant visual perturbations, supporting the robustness of intent-aware visual attenuation beyond simulation.

AI.brief_summary: DIVA 为 VLA 策略提出「先锚定后衰减」的双空间视觉衰减模块，用高层任务意图与低层视觉证据估计逐 patch 相关性锚点，在骨干入口重加权视觉 token 并持续衰减骨干内低相关视觉状态，在 LIBERO 与真实扰动场景报告成功率提升。
AI.relevance_reason: 其按意图筛选、衰减视觉 token 的做法，可能与 LVR 中「视觉证据筛选」及内部视觉状态保留多少的机制相关，可供核查相关性锚点是否能抑制信息坍缩或实现动态证据取舍；但工作场景为 VLA 策略而非生成式 latent 推理。
